low.label: Low — thin, circular, or mostly inferential evidence

moderate.label: Moderate — multiple independent indicators, but direct evidence missing

moderate-to-high.label: Moderate-to-High — strong indicators with some direct evidence

very-high.label: Very High — direct evidence exists and alternatives strongly contradicted

hypotheses.label: State pre-positioning against AI-transformed environments
hypotheses.description: Sophisticated nation-state actors are deliberately pre-positioning attacks against AI infrastructure and AI-transformed enterprise workflows as a strategic investment.
hypotheses.assessment: Holds at moderate-to-high. PLA doctrinal evidence (E16/E17) plus GTG-1002 detail (E11/E27/E39/E75) and second Vietnam campaign (E58) align motive, means, and partial trace. No public attribution yet of pre-positioning specifically against AI orchestration layers in critical infrastructure.
counterevidence: Multi-year passage with no further GTG-class disclosures
PLA doctrine remaining theoretical without operational expression
No attributable nation-state campaign explicitly targeting AI orchestration layers as objective (vs. using AI as tool against conventional targets)
hypotheses.watchFor: Compromise of widely-used MCP server with payload structured for selective behavioral modification or backdoor activation

hypotheses.label: Criminal opportunistic exploitation of AI-adoption gap
hypotheses.description: Threat actors are opportunistically exploiting the AI-adoption gap, primarily via supply chain attacks — economically rational, not strategically planned.
hypotheses.assessment: Strong and currently dominant pattern. TeamPCP target mix (E1/E2/E21), Mini-Shai-Hulud credential scope (E20), Hugging Face trojan pattern (E12), Mercor-via-LiteLLM (E3), and now postmark-mcp (E68) all fit. AI packages and MCP servers are basket members, not exclusive focus.
counterevidence: A supply-chain wave targeting exclusively AI-pure components with no non-AI targets in the same campaigns
Disappearance of opportunistic mass-compromise patterns
TeamPCP-class actors shifting to AI-only target lists
hypotheses.watchFor: Target selection narrowing to AI-pure components only

hypotheses.label: AI-as-tool is the dominant pattern, not AI-as-target
hypotheses.description: Most observed 'AI attack' activity is AI being used as an attacker tool, not attacks on AI itself; the target taxonomy is being conflated.
hypotheses.assessment: Very strong. OpenAI principal investigator on record: 'incremental efficiency gains, not new capabilities' (E55). Storm-2139 stolen-credential pattern (E26), GTG-1002 commodity orchestration (E27), Splunk 'not autonomous yet' (E60) all reinforce.
counterevidence: Emergence of novel-class attacks specifically targeting AI infrastructure with no conventional analog
Vendor primary sources beginning to revise upward on capability assessment
Documented adversary capabilities exceeding what stolen-credential-on-frontier-model can produce
hypotheses.watchFor: Custom adversarial AI tooling with capability ceiling above current frontier models

hypotheses.label: Research and PoC traffic inflating in-the-wild numbers
hypotheses.description: A meaningful share of reported 'AI threat' volume is research, PoC, and red-team disclosure mis-classified as in-the-wild adversary activity.
hypotheses.assessment: Moderate, slightly weakening. Picus 2025 Red Report empirical finding of no AI-driven malware uptick (E30) and predicted-vs-realized gap (E36/E37) still support. But MCPTox empirical attack success (E62), Endor MCP vulnerability prevalence (E63), and postmark-mcp (E68) show the gap is closing.
counterevidence: Picus or equivalent telemetry showing year-over-year uptick in AI-driven malware techniques
Attributable adversary operations against agentic systems exceeding red-team disclosures by clear margin
Production AI infrastructure compromises with adversary attribution increasing
hypotheses.watchFor: Independent telemetry diverging from research-corpus pattern

hypotheses.label: Vendor and media narrative inflation
hypotheses.description: Vendor and media incentives inflate ordinary supply chain attacks and traditional fraud into 'AI threats' for funding and coverage reasons.
hypotheses.assessment: Material contributing factor. $4.1B AI-security VC funding (E31), Gartner $172B projection (E32), 7AI $130M Series A (E33) establish a structural incentive. Frame divergence on same incidents (E43) and headline packaging (E42/E44) show it operating. Partially offset by primary vendor sources actively deflating (E55/E60).
counterevidence: Picus-equivalent empirical measurements aligning with vendor projections
Independent academic measurement studies showing comparable threat volumes to vendor claims
AI security spending growing without corresponding incident growth
hypotheses.watchFor: Convergence of empirical telemetry and vendor projections

hypotheses.label: Opportunistic piggybacking on AI-adjacent libraries
hypotheses.description: Real, novel-class attacks against AI infrastructure exist but are still rare; opportunistic supply-chain piggybacking on AI libraries is the dominant pattern.
hypotheses.assessment: Strong. Best single descriptor of current supply-chain reality. Now extends explicitly to MCP via postmark-mcp (E68). 188% YoY malicious packages (E19), Mini-Shai-Hulud broad credential scope (E20), bulk scope targeting pattern (E21) all reinforce.
counterevidence: Strategic concentration of attacks on a specific AI sub-component
Disappearance of mass-campaign target mixing
Sophisticated payloads specifically designed to persist past inference time

hypotheses.label: Adversaries in capability-building / scoping phase
hypotheses.description: A fraction of adversary activity reflects deliberate capability-building — toolchains, models, infrastructure — not yet deployed at scale. The 'scoping phase' framing for forward-looking analysis.
hypotheses.assessment: Strengthened. GTG-1002 (E11/E27/E39/E75) is the cleanest example of an adversary building orchestration capability from commodity components. Hallucination ceiling (E28) limits scaling speed. PLA doctrinal trajectory (E16) is the strongest forward-looking signal. MCPTox empirical attack success (E62) shows the playbook is available.
counterevidence: 12-24 more months passing with no further GTG-class adversary capability disclosures
Hallucination ceiling proving binding for adversary operations at scale
Capability ceiling on stolen-API-key access proving sufficient deterrent
hypotheses.watchFor: Adversary tooling that explicitly works around hallucination limitations
